concept: US-person access to perpetuals and US-regulated perp fees

claims.text: Lighter's Terms of Service state its services are not available to persons or entities who reside in, are located in, are incorporated in or have a registered office or principal place of business in the United States, Canada, the United Kingdom, China, North Korea, Russia, Ukraine, Cuba, Iran, Venezuela, Sudan, Belarus, Myanmar or Syria, and allow the company to suspend or terminate access without prior notice on suspected unauthorized access to the API or other suspicious activity. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-22)

Geofencing alone is not a reliable control: CoinDesk, reporting on the Polymarket probe, says that although the prediction market blocks US IP addresses, legal experts said this alone may not be sufficient to comply with US regulations, and that aside from geofencing the only real way to prevent people in restricted countries from accessing a site is by requiring identification. Paradex's Restricted Persons terms key on 'US person' status (as defined under US securities and commodity futures laws), not only IP location. (medium confidence)

Geofencing alone is not a reliable control: CoinDesk's reporting on the Polymarket probe quotes legal experts that blocking US IP addresses alone may not be sufficient to comply with US regulations, and that aside from geofencing the only real way to prevent people in restricted countries from accessing a site is by requiring identification. This is an analogy from prediction markets; offshore perp terms such as Paradex's key on 'US person' status (as defined under US securities and commodity futures laws), not only location. (medium confidence)

Reuters reported that Bitnomial is the only US platform offering perpetual futures via self-certification and that Coinbase self-certified 'perpetual-style' futures with five-year expiration dates and leverage of up to 10 times. On June 12, 2026 CFTC staff issued a no-action letter permitting Bitnomial and Coinbase Derivatives to convert certain existing perpetual-style digital commodity futures contracts into Perpetuals by removing their expiration dates. Bitnomial's filing BTNL 2026-64 (Updates to Rules 101 and 502 to Eliminate Expiration on Perpetual Futures Contracts) becomes effective on June 12, 2026. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-08-11)

Kraken's fee is a flat per-contract fee, so its cost in basis points depends on price and contract size. Kraken lists PBTCUCZ50 (Bitcoin) at 0.01 BTC per contract, and Bitnomial's self-certification confirms a contract size of 0.01 BTC; Kraken's all-in rate is $0.0113/contract per side. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-03)

Geofencing alone is a weak control, and evading it is a terms breach. CoinDesk's reporting on Polymarket says that although the prediction market blocks US IP addresses, legal experts said this alone may not be sufficient to comply with US regulations. Hyperliquid's terms prohibit using technologies such as VPNs, proxies, or other methods to conceal location, Paradex's terms prohibit the use of a VPN to circumvent applicable access restrictions, and Lighter says it may log IP addresses to enforce access restrictions. None of this is a statement about any individual's legal exposure. (medium confidence)

ICE (parent of the New York Stock Exchange) agreed with Trade XYZ to bring Trade XYZ's Hyperliquid perpetual futures to the US, pending regulatory approval. ICE would be the exclusive operator of Trade XYZ's regulated markets and intends to establish a new, dedicated, regulated retail market and clearing structure. Galaxy Research notes that US traders will get a separate, permissioned venue with its own clearing, and that the liquidity will not be shared with the existing HIP-3 markets, meaning the US venue will start from zero. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-29)

Bitnomial provides two methods for connecting and trading on the Exchange: Direct and Indirect. Direct Market Access (DMA) provides low-latency connectivity through private network connections, with AWS PrivateLink as the primary option. Its Binary (BTP) API is a low latency binary protocol for order entry and price feeds. The REST API is rate-limited to 200 requests per 5 minutes, and exceeding this rate results in HTTP 403 responses. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-22)

Hyperliquid enforces its US restriction at the front end, not the chain. As of November 2, 2026 the frontend at app.hyperliquid.xyz still showed its restricted-jurisdiction banner to a US connection, and the Terms of Service still restricted use by US persons. The L1 protocol underneath does not perform this check; it processes signed transactions from any wallet. Per the guide, Hyperliquid's own Terms of Service are the actual restriction, and the frontend IP check is one mechanism for enforcing them. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-02)

Coinbase Financial Markets has offered US customers CFTC-regulated perpetual futures since July 21, 2025 (nano Bitcoin and nano Ether at launch), with up to 10x intraday leverage on crypto. Coinbase's own announcement says fees are as low as 0.02% per contract. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-04-22)

Kalshi's perpetual futures fee schedule (submitted August 4, 2026, effective not before August 18, 2026) sets taker fees from 0.0400% at tier 0 down to 0.0100% at >= $1,000M of trailing perps plus prediction volume, and maker fees from 0.0200% at tier 0 to 0.0000% from >= $10M. The amended fee schedule applies the existing self-clearing member fee schedule to traders executing orders through an FCM; a proposed change filed on June 24, 2026 (charging a fee to FCM customers) did not take effect. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-08-04)

Kalshi's Temporary Perpetual Fee Rebate Program update (implemented on or after 5:00 PM ET on August 18, 2026) covers all Self-Clearing Members of Kalshi. Taker fees will be rebated down to 0.3 bps (0.003%) and makers net 0.3 bps (0.003%). The update remains in effect until the earlier of December 31, 2026, or a date on which Kalshi amends or terminates the Program, and Kalshi may end the Program at any time with one week's notice to all exchange participants. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-08-04)

Coinbase Derivatives' nano Bitcoin Perp Style future (BIP) is 0.01 BTC per contract. A broker page lists an initial expiration on the third Friday of December 2030 and exchange fees of $.10/contract. Coinbase's launch post quoted fees as low as 0.02% per contract, with a minimum of $0.15 charged per contract. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-30)

Coinbase's global perpetuals are not for US persons: Coinbase's derivatives page says its offering is available via Coinbase Advanced for retail traders in eligible non-US jurisdictions, and stock and commodity perpetual futures are available only to users in eligible jurisdictions and offered by Coinbase Bermuda Ltd. Coinbase's help page prices perpetual futures at 0.25% of notional and says the page does not apply to Coinbase Advanced, institutional clients, or US futures. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-22)

Robinhood's US perps charge a Robinhood commission of 0.005% of notional exposure plus a venue exchange fee of 0.005% of notional exposure, a liquidation fee of 0.05% of notional exposure and a $0 NFA regulatory fee (covered by Robinhood); these rates apply through December 31, 2026 and are subject to change. Funding windows occur every 8 hours and P&L is settled every 15 minutes. Leverage is up to 10x on BTC and ETH and 3x on SOL, XRP, DOGE, ADA, LINK and HYPE. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-22)

The Crypto Perps trading fee on all eligible instruments is waived from October 27 to November 26, 2026. The Exchange post lists a 100% waiver on maker fees, taker fees, DCM pass-through fees and liquidation fees. Standard funding payments still apply. New perpetual contract traders get a US$50 fee rebate voucher from November 27, valid for 7 days. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-27)

Coinbase Financial Markets has offered US customers CFTC-regulated perpetual futures since July 21, 2025. Coinbase's 2025 announcement quotes fees as low as 0.02% per contract, with a minimum of $0.15 charged per contract. Coinbase's derivatives page lists nano Bitcoin Perp with a contract size of 0.01 Bitcoin. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-22)

Crypto.com and OG.com launched regulated crypto perpetuals for the US market on October 27, 2026, with up to 5x leverage. OG.com operates a CFTC-regulated exchange and clearinghouse and futures commission merchant, which is connected to the Crypto.com Introducing Broker. Robinhood's US crypto perps rollout has an eight-contract lineup offering no-expiry trading through Robinhood Derivatives and Bitstamp. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-28)

Kalshi's CFTC-filed schedule for perps charges self-clearing members a taker fee of 0.0400% at tier 0 falling to 0.0100% at >= $1,000M, and a maker fee of 0.0200% falling to 0.0000% from >= $10M. An October filing adds a separate FCM Member schedule with crypto taker fees of 0.1200% (tier 0), 0.1000% (>= $100K), 0.0600% (>= $1M) and 0.0200% (>= $10M). The FCM fee schedule applies the same maker fees, and the same taker fees at Tiers 3 through 5, as the self-clearing member fee schedule, and each FCM member remains free to set the commissions and fees it charges its own customers. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-15)

Kalshi's October filing also sets lower rates for non-crypto perps: its Energy Perpetuals Exchange Fee Schedule lists a tier 0 taker fee of 0.0080% and maker fee of 0.0040%, and its Foreign-Exchange Perpetuals Exchange Fee Schedule lists a tier 0 taker fee of 0.0056% and maker fee of 0.00280%. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-15)

Kalshi's Temporary Perpetual Fee Rebate Program applies to all Perps markets on the Exchange, including Perps referencing cryptocurrencies, metals, indices, energy, and foreign-exchange. Eligible Participants are all Self-Clearing Members of Kalshi, who receive monthly Rebates of 98% of all net taker and maker fees. The Program is effective not earlier than 5:00 PM ET on October 29, 2026 and continues until the earlier of December 31, 2026, or the date that Kalshi amends or terminates the Program. Kalshi's filing says the effect is a trading fee holiday for Self-Clearing Members. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-15)

Coinbase's Advanced Trade API supports trading for US derivatives products offered by Coinbase Financial Markets (order management, market data and futures-specific endpoints), and users apply for a futures account. The same guide says that during the introductory beta period, Coinbase is only charging 0.05% (the lowest Advanced Trade tier). (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-22)

Crypto.com's US perps trade on a CFTC-regulated exchange and clearinghouse that does business in the Crypto.com App under the brand Crypto.com | Derivatives North America (CDNA) and in a separate trader-focused App, with leverage up to 5x, and the final funding rate cannot be higher than +2% or lower than −2% for an eight-hour interval. Foris DAX Inc is the entity registered with NFA as an introducing broker. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-27)

Kalshi's Perps API mirrors its event-contract API under a `/margin` namespace, with endpoints for account balance and risk, funding (estimated and historical rates, plus payment history), fee tiers, subaccounts, and transfers between event-contract and margin balances. Production endpoints are 'rolling out member by member', with REST on the `external-api` hosts and WebSocket and FIX on separate perps hosts. The event-contract to margin transfer is not yet available (enabled with the production rollout), and `/margin/enabled` shows whether margin is on for an account. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-22)

Gibson Dunn says the risk controls it describes are principally associated with offshore and onchain trading venues, which generally are not available to US persons. CoinGape says Binance Futures, Bybit, Deribit, and OKX's international derivatives platform restrict US residents from using their international futures services. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-16)

US-based Kalshi users who have completed KYC verification are eligible to apply for perps access, and international availability may expand in the future. Applying involves a margin account application with a short questionnaire about trading experience and risk tolerance. Most retail users trade perpetuals currently through Kalshi Prime, a registered Futures Commission Merchant (FCM), while institutional participants may become Self-Clearing Members and clear directly with Kalshi Klear. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-22)

Kalshi documents a Perps API under a `/margin` namespace that mirrors its event-contract API. The production REST base URL is `https://external-api.kalshi.com/trade-api/v2/margin/` (rolling out member by member); WebSocket and FIX use separate perps hosts, and a lower-latency host serves fill and user_orders updates. Margin endpoints cover account balance and risk, funding (estimated and historical rates, plus payment history), fee tiers, and subaccounts. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-22)

CME filed suit on June 18, 2026 in the US District Court for the District of Columbia against the CFTC, challenging the May 29, 2026 order approving Kalshi's BTCPERP and the Policy Statement. If CME prevails, the court could vacate the Kalshi Order and Policy Statement and declare that digital commodity Perpetuals are 'swaps' rather than 'futures' under the CEA. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-06-18)

CFTC Chairman Michael Selig said crypto onchain platforms looking to offer derivatives to US retail traders can register as an exchange or partner with one that is already registered, pointing to Backpack, which earlier that week received three licenses for its US entry, as an example of the first route. He also explained why the agency considers single-stock perpetuals futures rather than swaps, saying funding payments are very similar to variation margin with other types of futures contracts and the contracts are structured as futures, not as a swap or a security-based swap. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-19)

Kalshi perp fees depend on account route. Kalshi's CFTC fee-schedule filing sets taker fees from 0.0400% at tier 0 to 0.0100% at >= $1,000M of 30D trailing perps plus prediction volume and maker fees from 0.0200% at tier 0 to 0.0000% from >= $10M, and says this section is available to all self-clearing members of the exchange. A third-party read of the live Base-rate selections displayed different taker schedules for Prime and self-clearing: below $100,000, Prime was 0.120% /12 bps taker and 0.020% /2 bps maker versus self-clearing 0.040% /4 bps taker and 0.020% /2 bps maker. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-21)

A single-author SSRN preprint reports that Kalshi launched the first CFTC-regulated perpetual futures on 3 June 2026, and that through 20 September 2026 39% of BTC and 48% of ETH notional was executed in resting quotes of a fixed dollar size taken in full by orders of the same size. When the fee schedule went live on 24 June, venue-wide volume collapsed by 80-92% within hours and returned about forty hours later with ticket volume three to five times higher. The author says the evidence is consistent with volume that exists because it is costless to produce rather than because it serves a trading purpose. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-09-22)

An SSRN working paper finds that through 20 September 2026 (26.3 million trades, $47.2 billion) 39% of BTC and 48% of ETH notional was executed in resting quotes of a fixed dollar size taken in full by orders of the same size. When the fee schedule went live on 24 June, venue-wide volume collapsed by 80-92% within hours and returned about forty hours later with ticket volume three to five times higher; the metals contracts show no fixed-size flow. The author says the evidence is consistent with volume that exists because it is costless to produce rather than because it serves a trading purpose. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-09-22)

Hyperliquid's Terms of Use (clause 1.6) bar 'Restricted Persons', defined to include persons or entities that reside in, are located in, are incorporated in or have a registered office in the United States of America or Ontario, Canada. Reuters likewise reports that offshore platforms like Hyperliquid typically try to restrict US users. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-22)

Hyperliquid does not currently offer its trading platform to US users and enforces geo-blocking for US and Ontario, Canada residents; Hyperliquid Policy Center CEO Jake Chervinsky said the goal is for regulators to interpret existing rules favourably or create new ones that would allow regulated firms to offer perpetual futures using markets built on Hyperliquid. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-08-12)

Hyperliquid co-founder and CEO Jeff Yan said that Americans using a VPN to access the exchange violate its terms of service, and that legal US access depends on regulators deciding that onchain technology fits CFTC principles. A VPN therefore creates a terms breach, not legal access. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-19)

Paradex's Restricted Persons page excludes the United States (plus US associated territories such as Puerto Rico, Guam and the US Virgin Islands), Canada, and any 'US person' as defined under US securities and commodity futures laws; users represent on an ongoing basis that they are not a Restricted Person. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-22)

On May 29, 2026 the CFTC approved KalshiEX's bitcoin perpetual contract BTCPERP as a futures contract under Section 5c(c)(4) and Regulation 40.3. The same day it issued a policy statement on listing perpetual contracts, a staff advisory on 24/7 trading and clearing, and an interpretive letter and no-action position for Coinbase Financial Markets (CFTC Letter No. 26-17). (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-05-29)

The CFTC policy statement encourages DCMs that wish to list perpetual contracts referencing asset classes not covered by the Order (such as agricultural products, precious metals, equity securities, narrow-based security indexes) to voluntarily submit them for Regulation 40.3 review and approval. The BTCPERP contract approved is a perpetual contract that references the spot price of bitcoin. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-05-29)

A CFTC interpretive letter confirms that Deribit FZE perpetuals (Deribit is an affiliated foreign board of trade regulated by the Dubai Virtual Assets Regulatory Authority) may be categorized as 'foreign futures' under Regulation 30.1, letting Coinbase Financial Markets offer US customers access to them. The interpretation is limited to perpetual contracts structured similarly to the Deribit Perpetuals and based on digital commodities with deep, active, and continuous spot market trading. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-05-29)

In an April report, Reuters described US perps as being in a regulatory gray area, neither banned nor explicitly approved. It said Bitnomial is the only US platform offering perpetual futures via self-certification and that Coinbase self-certified 'perpetual-style' futures with five-year expiration dates and leverage of up to 10 times; Kraken's parent company was acquiring Bitnomial for up to $550 million. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-04-22)

Kraken launched CFTC-regulated US perpetual futures on Kraken Pro; the contracts are listed on Bitnomial (owned by Kraken's parent Payward), and Kraken's support page lists 16 contracts at launch (for example PBTCUC). Bitnomial's self-certification shows PBTCUC is a cash-settled perpetual futures contract with a contract size of 0.01 BTC referenced to the CF Bitcoin Mid-Price Spot Rate. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-30)

Kraken Derivatives US charges a flat per-contract all-in fee of $0.0113 per side for Bitnomial-listed perps ($0.0003 commission + $0.001 exchange/clearing + $0.01 NFA); round-turn is double. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-30)

Bitnomial describes its perps as replicating the full economic design of offshore perpetuals, on the same unified exchange and clearinghouse as futures, options and spot, and as the first and only CFTC-regulated exchange accepting digital assets as margin collateral. Its API surface is reported (by a third-party API directory profile) as a real-time WebSocket market-data feed, a low-latency binary order-entry protocol (BTP), and a FIX 4.4 API with dropcopy, with REST authentication using HMAC-SHA256 request signing. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-22)

Hyperliquid enforces the US restriction at its web frontend. As of November 2, 2026 the frontend at app.hyperliquid.xyz still showed its restricted-jurisdiction banner to a US connection, and the Terms govern the website-hosted Interface. One affiliate guide adds that the L1 protocol itself does not perform IP-based geo-blocking, a distinction it calls purely technical that does not amount to a statement about what is or is not permitted. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-02)

Lighter's Terms of Service cover its website, Interface, Protocol, API and LIT Token, and state the services are not available to persons or entities that reside in, are located in, are incorporated in or have a registered office or principal place of business in the United States of America, Canada, the United Kingdom, China, North Korea, Russia, Ukraine, Cuba, Iran, Venezuela, Sudan, Belarus, Myanmar or Syria. Lighter may suspend or terminate access without prior notice on suspected unauthorized access to the API or other suspicious activity. A fetch of the Lighter app returned a banner reading 'You’re accessing Lighter from a restricted jurisdiction.' (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-22)

Paradex does not serve Restricted Persons: restricted territories include Canada, the United States and US associated territories, and any 'US person' as defined under US commodity futures and securities laws (an individual resident in the United States, or an entity organized under US law or with its principal place of business in the United States). Users represent on an ongoing basis that they are not a Restricted Person. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-22)

In a letter dated September 29, 2026 to Hyperliquid Labs co-founder Jeff Yan, the House Oversight Committee requested documents and information to better understand how Hyperliquid implements identity verification for domestic and international account holders, enforces geographic restrictions, and detects anomalous trading activity, as soon as possible but no later than October 13, 2026. A Hyperliquid Labs spokesperson told The Block that the company was aware of Representative James Comer's request and reviewing it. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-09-29)

On May 29, 2026 the CFTC approved KalshiEX's BTCPERP as a futures contract under Section 5c(c)(4) of the Commodity Exchange Act and Regulation 40.3. The Order's scope is limited to the BTCPERP Contract and similarly structured perpetual futures referencing bitcoin or other digital commodities, and Katten says the related interpretation does not extend to other asset classes. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-05-29)

The CFTC Policy Statement on listing perpetual contracts (91 Fed Reg. 33160, June 3, 2026) indicates that perpetuals referencing assets outside the scope of the Kalshi Order, such as agricultural products, precious metals, equity securities and narrow-based security indexes, should be submitted for case-by-case review and approval under Regulation 40.3 before being listed on a DCM. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-06-03)

A CFTC staff letter of May 29, 2026 confirms that the perpetual contracts described in it may be categorized as foreign futures under Regulation 30.1, and Katten reports that the Market Participants Division also gave no-action relief permitting Coinbase Financial Markets to post customer digital assets with its foreign broker affiliate, Coinbase Bermuda Limited, as margin, subject to nine conditions. A staff advisory (CFTC Letter No. 26-16) sets expectations for 24/7 trading and clearing. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-05-29)

CFTC staff no-action letters let US exchanges convert long-dated perpetual-style futures into true perpetuals. Gibson Dunn dates a no-action letter of June 12, 2026 permitting Bitnomial and Coinbase Derivatives to convert existing perpetual-style digital commodity futures into Perpetuals by removing their expiration dates. CFTC Letter No. 26-29 (October 03, 2026) addresses removal of expiration dates from existing broad-based security index perpetual-style futures contracts, which had long-dated expiration dates of up to 25 years. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-03)

CME's suit against the CFTC (case 1:26-cv-02157, filed June 18, 2026, listed as ongoing) is before Judge Colleen Kollar-Kotelly. CME did not ask for a preliminary injunction. On September 2 the CFTC moved to dismiss, relying on CME chairman Terrence Duffy's statement on the July earnings call that perpetual futures do not appeal to CME's customers. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-05)

The Capital Markets Alliance Association is challenging the CFTC's single-stock perpetual futures approvals. District Judge Valerie Caproni denied a temporary restraining order on November 3 that would have halted stock perpetual futures on Kalshi, Coinbase Derivatives and Bitnomial, but wrote that the group 'is likely to succeed on the merits' of its claim that the agency lacks statutory authority. Coinbase, Kalshi, Payward, DRW Holdings, Jump Trading and Paradigm filed briefs backing the CFTC, and CME sought permission to submit an amicus brief in support of the alliance. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-10)

The CFTC argues in CME v. Selig that if CME prevails, Kalshi and every other exchange could relist the same contracts as swaps under Rule 40.2 and keep trading them 'almost instantly'. This describes the CFTC's litigation position, made to defeat a standing argument, not a court finding. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-09-16)

Kalshi, Coinbase Derivatives and Bitnomial filed single-stock perps for CFTC review on September 18, and the CFTC let the 45-day review period lapse without a written order. CFTC Chairman Michael Selig announced the approval, saying the contracts passed the agency's review without objection. Kalshi was listing four single-stock perpetuals on Qualcomm, McDonald's, Amgen and Costco by November 4, with maximum leverage of 4.9 times. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-04)

Payward (Kraken's parent) announced on September 16, 2026 that it intends to deploy onchain perpetual futures markets for US clients, starting with Hyperliquid HIP-3 markets; Bitnomial, Payward's CFTC-regulated exchange and clearinghouse, would be the HIP-3 deployer. Only accounts onboarded by NinjaTrader and on both NinjaTrader and Bitnomial's allowlists could trade. Hyperliquid said it intends to make Payward the first CFTC-regulated deployer on its HIP-3 markets. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-26)

Hyperliquid Strategies (Nasdaq-listed, ticker PURR) disclosed on November 5, 2026 an application for US futures commission merchant (FCM) registration. The application remains pending; if approved, the subsidiary (HypeStrat Markets) could maintain US customer accounts for permissioned perpetual futures markets operating under Hyperliquid's proposed HIP-3 framework. FCM registration would not independently authorize the proposed trading venues or their derivatives contracts. The initiative does not represent regulatory approval for Hyperliquid's existing decentralized exchange, which currently restricts US users. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-05)

Kraken Derivatives US charges a flat all-in $0.0113 per contract per side on Bitnomial-listed perpetual futures: $0.0003 commission, $0.001 exchange/clearing and $0.01 NFA. USD only collateral is accepted at launch, and a $10 liquidation fee applies if trading perpetual futures only. The fee page was last updated October 30, 2026. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-30)

Bitnomial's PBTCUC contract has a contract size of 0.01 BTC, a tick size of $5 per BTC and a tick value of $0.05 per contract; Kraken's all-in rate on Bitnomial-listed perps is $0.0113/contract per side. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-30)

Backpack announced on November 16, 2026 CFTC approval for a Designated Contract Market (DCM) and Derivatives Clearing Organization (DCO), and Markets Media reports that it secured an FCM license and NFA membership. Backpack says US users will be able to trade crypto perpetual futures on a leveraged basis 24/7, use both fiat and crypto assets as collateral, enjoy cross-margin across their various positions, and access Backpack's global liquidity in one unified order book. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-18)

Funding cadence is stated differently across US venues. Bitnomial's REST docs say funding rates are calculated and applied at 8-hour intervals (00:00, 08:00, and 16:00 UTC). Kraken's launch blog says a funding payment is exchanged every 8 hours (CT), but Kraken's support article says payments are aggregated and settled as a single cash adjustment at 3:00 pm CT daily. Robinhood settles P&L every 15 minutes. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-22)

Kraken's developer guide says US Perps is accessed through three APIs: FIX 4.4 order entry (logon with a FIX API key, an HMAC-SHA512 password signature and a nonce), SBE (Simple Binary Encoding) market data including order-by-order (L3) books, and a FIX 4.4 drop copy. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-22)

Coinbase's Advanced Trade API supports trading for US derivatives products offered by Coinbase Financial Markets at order-management, market-data and futures-specific endpoints, and applying for a futures account is required. Coinbase Derivatives says its broker distribution partners provide expanded market access, with Interactive Brokers among those listed. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-22)

Zero-fee and low-fee US terms are time-limited, so a strategy costed on them needs re-costing. The Crypto Perps trading fee waiver runs from October 27 to November 26, 2026. Kalshi's rebate program update remains in effect until the earlier of December 31, 2026, or a date on which Kalshi amends or terminates the Program, and Kalshi may end the Program at any time with one week's notice to all exchange participants. Robinhood's rates apply through December 31, 2026 and are subject to change. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-22)

Hyperliquid's Terms of Use (last updated June 15, 2026, clause 1.6) bar 'Restricted Persons' from the Interface, defined to include persons or entities that reside in, are located in, are incorporated in, or have a registered office in the United States of America or Ontario, Canada. Clause 3.1.5 also prohibits using technologies such as VPNs, proxies, or other methods to conceal location. MetaMask's perps-DEX guide independently reports that Hyperliquid restricts users in the United States and Ontario (Canada). (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-22)

Hyperliquid co-founder and CEO Jeff Yan said that Americans who use a VPN to reach the exchange violate its terms of service, and that legal US access depends on regulators concluding that onchain technology fits CFTC core principles. A VPN therefore adds a terms breach and does not make access permitted under the terms. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-19)

Lighter's Terms of Service (covering its website, Interface, Protocol, API and LIT Token) say the services are not available to persons or entities who reside in, are located in, are incorporated in, or have a registered office or principal place of business in the United States of America, Canada, the United Kingdom, China, North Korea, Russia, Ukraine, Cuba, Iran, Venezuela, Sudan, Belarus, Myanmar or Syria. They also say Lighter may log the IP address used through the Interface to enforce access restrictions. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-22)

Paradex's Terms of Service bar any 'US person' as defined under US commodity futures and securities laws (for an individual, a resident of the United States; for an entity, one organized under US law or with its principal place of business in the United States). They say Paradex does not make exceptions and prohibit use of a VPN to circumvent access restrictions. Its Restricted Persons page also lists Canada, the United States and US associated territories (Micronesia, Guam, Marshall Islands, Northern Mariana Islands, Puerto Rico, Palau, US Minor Outlying Islands and US Virgin Islands). (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-22)

GRVT's Restricted Jurisdictions page (August 3, 2026) bans persons residing, located, incorporated or otherwise established in the United States of America including its territories such as Puerto Rico and Guam, and in the Republic of Singapore, Hong Kong and others. Aster's Terms and Conditions list the United States of America among its 'Prohibited Jurisdictions' with Canada, the United Kingdom, China and others. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-22)

Kraken Derivatives US (NinjaTrader Clearing, LLC, a CFTC-registered Futures Commission Merchant) offers perpetuals on Kraken Pro, in the same futures wallet as Kraken's CME-listed contracts. Kraken's support article lists 16 perpetual futures contracts at launch (for example PBTCUC). A $10 liquidation fee applies if trading perpetual futures only; with other futures positions the standard rate applies to all liquidation events: $25 for the first, $50 for each subsequent event. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-03)

Kraken's US Futures Fees page (last updated October 30, 2026) lists an all-in $0.0113/contract per side for Bitnomial-listed perps ($0.0003 commission, $0.001 exchange/clearing, $0.01 NFA). Bitnomial's fee page lists $0.0007 for Participants / $0.0010 for Non-Participants per side per Minimum Contract. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-30)

A Wayback snapshot of Kraken's US Futures Fees page (stamped 'Last updated: June 15, 2026') shows an all-in $0.15/contract per side ($0.03 commission, $0.10 exchange/clearing, $0.02 NFA), while the current page shows $0.0113/contract per side. CoinGape also cites $0.15 per contract per side for Kraken's Bitnomial perps, so sources quoting $0.15 are out of date relative to the current Kraken page. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-30)

Coinbase Derivatives, LLC's fee schedule effective August 17, 2026 charges fees per side per contract, and lists $0.10 and $0.01 for nano Bitcoin Perp Futures (BIP) and nano Ether Perp Futures (ETP). This is the exchange's own schedule, separate from a broker's all-in quote. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-08-17)

For Crypto Perps, the US launch offers two limited-time incentives for eligible users: the trading fee on all eligible instruments is waived from October 27 to November 26, 2026 (standard funding payments still apply), and a US$50 fee rebate voucher for new perpetual contract traders follows from November 27, valid for 7 days. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-22)

Bitnomial's self-certification BTNL 2026-123 (filed October 22, 2026) creates Direct Access and Indirect Access Participant classes. An Indirect Access Participant is a customer of its Sponsoring Member, is admitted through the Sponsoring Member's certification, accesses the Exchange solely through the Sponsoring Member's systems, and is recognized as a member for Perpetual Futures. Bitnomial says having two classes allows the Exchange to run incentive programs and differentiated fee structures for Participants in accordance with their membership class. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-22)

A third-party API directory reports that Bitnomial publishes a public HTTPS REST API (products, orders, fills, block trades, indexes, funding rates, market stats) and a real-time WebSocket market-data feed (trade, book, block, status channels), with REST authentication using HMAC-SHA256 request signing. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-22)

Hyperliquid-based US markets are announced, not live: two US plans have been named, both subject to regulatory approval and both without a date. Payward's plan (announced September 16, 2026) has Bitnomial as HIP-3 deployer, and only accounts onboarded by NinjaTrader and on both NinjaTrader and Bitnomial's allowlists could trade. The other, announced October 29, 2026, has Intercontinental Exchange operate a separate regulated US market for Trade XYZ's Hyperliquid-based markets; Bloomberg says ICE and Trade.xyz are planning a new market with its own clearing, know-your-customer and anti-money laundering systems. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-02)

CME filed suit on June 18, 2026 in the US District Court for the District of Columbia against the CFTC and Chairman Selig, challenging the Kalshi Order and the Policy Statement and arguing that Perpetuals are swaps, not futures; Gibson Dunn said the litigation remains pending as of the date of its publication. FOW (11th November, 2026) says CME has already brought a separate lawsuit against the CFTC over its approval of cryptocurrency perpetual contracts. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-11)

A second challenge targets single-stock perps: the Capital Markets Alliance filed suit in the US District Court for the Southern District of New York seeking to vacate the CFTC's approval of perpetual derivatives on individual US stocks. The CFTC let its 45-day review window lapse on Nov. 2 without objecting to the Sept. 18 applications from KalshiEX, Coinbase Derivatives and Bitnomial Exchange, which under its rules counts as approval. Coinbase, Kalshi, Payward, DRW, Jump Trading and Paradigm filed an amicus brief on Nov. 9 urging the court to reject the preliminary injunction the alliance is seeking, and CME filed a motion seeking permission to submit an amicus brief in support of the alliance. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-11)

US venues use different funding cadences. Kraken's launch blog describes an 8-hour funding rate, while its support article says payments are aggregated and settled as a single cash adjustment at 3:00 pm CT daily. Kraken's comparison page says Coinbase's funding rate accrues hourly and settles twice daily, and Gibson Dunn notes that funding intervals vary by venue and product, with payments commonly exchanged at one-hour to eight-hour intervals. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-22)
